title: Where AI fit in my solo Godot project: code analysis and wide-screen background art
author: BallzyTheGame
selftext:
Hi everyone. I am a solo dev, and my game Ballzy is a PvP block puzzler with a demo live on Steam right now.

Since this sub is about AI in game development, here is exactly where AI fit into my project.

Code analysis, not code writing. I used AI to analyse the code I had already written.

Background artwork. When the project moved from the Android version to the PC version, AI assistance was used for the background artwork that a wide screen needs.

The rest of the pipeline is plain Godot. The game is written in Godot, the scenes are drawn with the draw() function, only the ball uses a shader, and the effects are gathered on the GPU side to balance CPU and GPU load.

The demo has 5 Classic games, the first 10 Puzzle levels and 3 Battle matches. The full game is coming November 2026.

Steam page and demo: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5144960/?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_medium=organic\_social&utm\_campaign=steam\_next\_fest\_oct\_2026&utm\_content=aigamedev\_post](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5144960/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=steam_next_fest_oct_2026&utm_content=aigamedev_post)

Happy to talk about the Godot side or the AI side, whichever is more useful.

comments.author: barret232hxc
comments.body: man the idea of asychronous multiplayer games like this has me fascinated, I didn't even know it was a thing until just recently. I wasn't on the backpack battles bandwagon, but I love seeing how people are taking that concept if I understand correctly you can play real people's snapshots?

replies.author: BallzyTheGame
replies.body:
Thanks, man! In battle mode, you can play in turns but in a closed bidding system where turns resolve for both players at the same time. You can challenge a specific player but the game can also choose the player for you but these are not frozen snapshots but allocated game rooms so whenever you join someone's game, you'll be the only one fighting. 

However the classic mode is almost what you described. You score, then others try to beat your score and whoever has the highest score will have that map forever. Give it a try!
